title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook accrues phUSD debt at a fixed 1:1 USDS-to-debt ratio while the dispatcher's eventual realisable USDC is at the mercy of the sUSDS/waUSDC pool and waUSDC redeem rate — debt can systematically exceed realisable USDC
description:
The economic invariant the system implicitly relies on is: the phUSD mint debt accrued at dispatch time approximates the USDC that the dispatcher will eventually deliver to batchMinter via the donation/swap/redeem path. The hook computes added = amount * ratio / 100 where amount is the USDS quantity (18 decimals) passed to dispatch. phUSD is then minted to recipient on pull() for mintDebt units. There is no link, on-chain or off-chain in the hook, between mintDebt and the realised USDC. The realised USDC depends on (a) sUSDS ERC4626 share price at dispatch; (b) sUSDS/waUSDC Balancer V3 pool spot at pool() time; (c) waUSDC Aave-wrapper redeem rate at pool() time; (d) USDC's market price vs USDS.

Because ratio is fixed and mintDebt accrues per-dispatch with no rebasing, the debt can diverge from realisable USDC in either direction. The most damaging direction is debt > realisable USDC: sUSDS/USDC pool depeg, waUSDC redemption discount, or a USDC depeg will leave the pooler unable to deliver enough USDC to batchMinter while the hook still mints the full phUSD debt to recipient.

Additionally, the hook accrues debt on EVERY dispatch (including dispatches where batchDonationSize == 0, batchMinter unset, or swapPool/usdc/waUsdc unconfigured), in which case zero USDC is ever produced.

Re-validation note (yield-claim-nft-07, HEAD 1bb956c): Hook unchanged. BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch and donation block unchanged (only line numbers shifted forward by ~3 lines due to new import). Finding carries forward. Additionally noted: the new migrateMint function does NOT call _dispatch and so does NOT trigger the hook — confirmed safe on that axis (migrations do not inflate phUSD debt).
exploit_path:
Scenario A — debt > realisable USDC (loss to phUSD holders / pool):
1. 100,000 USDS worth of NFTs are minted via BalancerPoolerV2. Hook accrues mintDebt += 100,000 * ratio/100 (e.g., 50,000 phUSD at ratio=50).
2. Before pool() runs, USDC depegs to $0.95 (historical precedent: March 2023). sUSDS/waUSDC pool repricing reflects the depeg: 50,000 sUSDS in the donation swap yields waUSDC redeemable for ~47,500 USDC.
3. pool() executes, batchMinter receives 47,500 USDC.
4. Owner / recipient calls pull(); 50,000 phUSD is minted to recipient against an effectively realised value of 47,500 USDC — phUSD is overissued by 2,500 units (5%).

Scenario B — mintDebt accrual without donation execution (silent over-issuance):
1. Owner sets batchDonationSize = 0.
2. Users mint NFTs over months; mintDebt accrues to, say, 1,000,000 phUSD.
3. None of the sUSDS is ever converted to USDC.
4. Owner sets recipient and calls pull(); 1,000,000 phUSD is freshly minted with zero USDC backing produced through the donation path.
mainnet_realism: USDC has depegged historically (SVB, March 2023, to $0.87 briefly). sUSDS does not currently have a 1:1 peg to USDC — it is yield-bearing and appreciates against USDS. Aave waUSDC ERC4626 redeems near 1:1 with USDC modulo accrued interest.
recommendation: Either (a) recompute phUSD debt in pull() from the actual realised USDC delivered to batchMinter; OR (b) require that whenever the donation phase is disabled, the hook is replaced by DefaultDispatchHook; OR (c) cap pull() by an oracle-derived sUSDS->USDC fair value.
severity_rationale: Carry-forward from report-6 (Medium). Decoupled-ledger design — phUSD can be over-minted vs realised USDC backing. Materialises only on owner-driven pull() and depends on configuration choices (external requirement). Medium per C4.
poc_notes: PoC from report-6 still applies — hook and donation phase byte-identical at HEAD 1bb956c. Original PoC: 4 scenarios pass demonstrating debt/realised-USDC divergence.
